surgeries.name: Breast-conserving surgery
surgeries.indication: Early-stage breast cancer suitable for breast conservation where clear margins and acceptable cosmetic outcome are achievable.

Pre-op.text: Confirm diagnosis with triple assessment
Mammogram and ultrasound
Core biopsy confirmation
MRI in selected cases
MDT discussion
Discuss breast conservation versus mastectomy
Discuss radiotherapy requirement
Discuss re-excision risk
Localisation planning if impalpable lesion

Operative.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy when indicated
Cavity shave margins are performed based on surgeon preference.

Post-op.text: Discuss re-excision if margins are involved
Refer for systemic therapy when indicated

surgeries.name: Mastectomy
surgeries.indication: Breast cancer requiring full breast removal because of extent of disease, patient preference, contraindication to conservation or risk-reduction planning.

Pre-op.text: Confirm diagnosis and extent of disease
Discuss reconstruction options and patient decision aids
Anaesthetic and comorbidity assessment
MDT treatment plan confirmation

Operative.text: Total mastectomy with planned incision and flap management
Sentinel node or axillary surgery when indicated
Drain placement according to surgeon preference

Post-op.text: Drain removal is based on output threshold and surgeon preference.

surgeries.name: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
surgeries.indication: Axillary staging for clinically node-negative or selected low-volume node-positive early breast cancer.

Pre-op.text: Axillary status is assessed with clinical examination and ultrasound when indicated.
Confirm nuclear medicine or tracer pathway
Consent for sentinel node biopsy and possible escalation

Operative.text: Dual tracer sentinel node localisation when available
Document node count and mapping success

Post-op.text: MDT discussion for positive sentinel nodes

surgeries.name: Axillary lymph node dissection
surgeries.indication: Therapeutic axillary clearance for selected patients with clinically significant nodal disease where de-escalation is not appropriate.

Pre-op.text: Confirm nodal disease and MDT recommendation
Discuss lymphoedema, numbness and shoulder morbidity
Baseline arm and shoulder assessment when available

Operative.text: Axillary clearance to agreed anatomical level
Identify and preserve key neurovascular structures where possible
Drain placement according to local practice

Post-op.text: Patients are monitored for lymphoedema and shoulder stiffness after surgery.

surgeries.name: Oncoplastic breast surgery
surgeries.indication: Breast-conserving cancer surgery using volume displacement or replacement techniques to preserve breast shape and oncological safety.

Pre-op.text: Cosmetic expectations, asymmetry and scarring are discussed during standard consent.
Photography and symmetry assessment when appropriate
Discuss radiotherapy effects and revision possibility

Operative.text: Wide local excision with planned oncoplastic closure
Specimen orientation and imaging when indicated

evidenceUpdates.title: Routine cavity shave margins may reduce re-excision risk
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Cavity shave margins are performed based on surgeon preference.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Routine cavity shave margins may reduce positive margin rates and re-excision rates in selected patients undergoing breast-conserving surgery.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: A Randomized Trial of Cavity Shave Margins in Breast Cancer
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Consider routine cavity shave margins in selected patients undergoing breast-conserving surgery, subject to local protocol review.

evidenceUpdates.title: Selected low-risk patients may avoid escalation of axillary surgery
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Axillary status is assessed with clinical examination and ultrasound when indicated.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Selected low-risk patients with limited nodal disease may not require escalation to more aggressive axillary surgery when other treatment factors are favourable.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Sentinel-Node Biopsy in Early Breast Cancer
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Review axillary management pathway for selected low-risk patients at MDT before escalation to axillary lymph node dissection.

evidenceUpdates.title: Earlier drain removal may be suitable for selected low-risk patients
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Drain removal is based on output threshold and surgeon preference.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Selected low-risk mastectomy patients may be suitable for earlier drain removal protocols without substantially increasing seroma risk.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Early Drain Removal After Breast Surgery
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Consider local audit or protocol review for earlier drain removal in selected low-risk patients.

evidenceUpdates.title: Structured counselling may improve expectation-setting
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Cosmetic expectations, asymmetry and scarring are discussed during standard consent.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Structured pre-operative counselling using patient-reported outcome data may improve expectation-setting and satisfaction after oncoplastic breast surgery.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Patient-reported outcomes after oncoplastic breast surgery
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Add a structured counselling checklist for symmetry, scarring, recovery time and revision possibility.

evidenceUpdates.title: Early physiotherapy may reduce shoulder morbidity
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Patients are monitored for lymphoedema and shoulder stiffness after surgery.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Early physiotherapy and structured patient education may reduce shoulder morbidity after axillary surgery.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Early physiotherapy after axillary lymph node dissection
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Add early physiotherapy referral and shoulder exercise education to the post-op pathway.

evidenceUpdates.title: Shorter radiotherapy pathways may suit selected patients
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Patients are referred for radiotherapy using the standard post-operative referral pathway.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Selected patients may be suitable for hypofractionated radiotherapy pathways after breast-conserving surgery where oncology criteria are met.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Hypofractionated radiotherapy for early breast cancer
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Add an MDT prompt to consider hypofractionated radiotherapy suitability during post-operative planning.

evidenceUpdates.title: Decision aids may improve reconstruction conversations
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: Reconstruction options are discussed during standard consent.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Structured decision aids may improve patient understanding of reconstruction timing, trade-offs and recovery expectations.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Decision aids for breast reconstruction after mastectomy
evidenceUpdates.suggestedAcceptedChange: Pilot a reconstruction decision aid before final operative consent for eligible patients.

evidenceUpdates.title: Routine MRI expansion is not flagged for this pathway
evidenceUpdates.currentPractice: MRI is used in selected cases based on clinical and imaging factors.
evidenceUpdates.newEvidenceShows: Current local selection criteria remain reasonable; no active pathway change is proposed from this update.
evidenceUpdates.articleTitle: Pre-operative MRI selection in early breast cancer
